summary: Use a small board-specific read use-case because the board owns cross-capability policy. Keep work-items and labels independent; the RSC page should only invoke an authenticated server-only read entrypoint.

tree.purpose: RSC route; parses URL filters and renders serializable board DTOs.
Server-only authenticated read entrypoint; verifies the actor and composes injected dependencies.
Pure orchestration and board policy: hide archived items, group by status, resolve visible labels, and omit unauthorized label attachments.
Minimal read ports for work-item summaries and label details; no persistence or framework imports.
Valibot schemas and DTOs for board input, groups, items, and visible labels.
Adapter behind the work-items public read contract; work-items owns its persistence and authorization behavior.
Adapter behind the labels public read contract; labels owns its persistence and visibility checks.
Server-side session/claims verification used by the DAL.
Redacted logging/telemetry helpers for unexpected board-read failures.
Fake-port tests for policy, grouping, label visibility, and failure outcomes.
Auth and composition tests for the server-only boundary.
RSC rendering tests for empty, grouped, and degraded label results.
Authenticated browser coverage using real work-item and label data.

flows: GET /board → app/board/page.tsx → src/dal/board/get-board.ts → verifyActor() → getBoard({ workItems, labels }, input, actor) → work-items read API and labels read API → board policy → BoardView.

The board use-case requests work items scoped to the actor, removes archived items, groups remaining items by status, collects referenced label IDs, requests label details through the labels public read contract, and attaches only labels the actor may view.
Work-items and labels never import each other or the board module; both expose independently versioned read contracts consumed through injected board ports.

A work-item mutation elsewhere invalidates its scoped RSC board cache tag; a label mutation invalidates the affected actor/tenant board tag. The board read remains RSC/DAL-owned and does not use TanStack Query.

decisions.choice: Introduce a narrow board read use-case and DAL entrypoint.
decisions.rationale: The page owns neither cross-capability policy nor authorization. Direct page composition would make the RSC entrypoint a business-policy layer; work-items calling labels would violate independence and change isolation.

decisions.choice: Board use-case depends only on local ports and domain types; composition occurs in the DAL/inbound layer.
decisions.rationale: This keeps persistence, Supabase, Next.js, React, and auth infrastructure out of pure orchestration.

decisions.choice: Verify the actor in the DAL, then re-check visibility through each capability’s trusted server API.
decisions.rationale: Proxy protection is insufficient, and the board must not trust client-provided actor or label visibility.

decisions.choice: Omit inaccessible label attachments and their metadata from the board DTO; do not expose existence or raw errors.
decisions.rationale: This is fail-closed for label data while allowing otherwise authorized work items to render.

decisions.choice: Treat capability auth/session failures and unexpected persistence failures as board-read failures; render the route error state and capture unexpected errors once with redacted context.
decisions.rationale: Partial capability failure must not produce misleading or security-sensitive output.

decisions.choice: Test policy with fake ports, adapters against their lowest transport boundary, DAL auth separately, and the complete flow in e2e.
decisions.rationale: Each test mocks only the boundary owned by the layer under test.

risks: The existing work-items and labels APIs must provide batch reads scoped to the actor; otherwise label resolution may cause N+1 queries or inconsistent authorization.
Cache tags must include the relevant tenant/actor scope and label dependencies; broad tags could leak freshness across users or tenants.
The UI must distinguish an empty board from an authorization/session failure without exposing capability-specific error details.
